section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the measures used in a single study (Study X, n=247) with female participants. Body mass index was assessed via self-reported height and weight, with a mean BMI of 30.53 (SD=10.38). Body appreciation was measured using the 13-item Body Appreciation Scale (BAS), which demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach's α=.93) in this sample. Sexual functioning was also assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), though the correlation between body appreciation and BMI is not reported in this excerpt.

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the measures used in a single study with 247 female participants (mean age 29.8 years, mean BMI 30.53). Participants completed the 13-item Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) to assess sexual functioning across six domains. Body mass index was calculated from self-reported height and weight. Table 1 presents descriptive statistics and correlations among all measures, showing a significant negative correlation between BAS score and BMI (r = -.22, p < .05).
